title: A Heart Means Recursion: Exploring Visual Meaning and Communication in VLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.36449v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Do vision-language models (VLMs) share our ability to communicate visually? We share preliminary findings, starting from a surprising observation: simple visual symbols like a red heart can strongly influence model behavior on seemingly unrelated tasks, such as steering models towards recursive solutions on simple coding problems. Notably, this steering effect is largely implicit, as models' direct interpretations and thinking traces about visual symbols diverge substantially from their observed behavior. In visual communication between models, this leads to a generation--interpretation gap: while models tend to send shape primitives that they (and humans) find intuitive, these visual cues often fail to steer other models. In further communication games involving abstract concepts and stories, models can creatively use visuals to transmit meaning to one another, although some communications remain non-intuitive to humans. translated_title: 一颗心形符号意味着递归：探索视觉语言模型中的视觉含义与交流
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）是否具备与我们相同的视觉交流能力？我们分享了初步研究发现，从一个令人惊讶的观察开始：简单的视觉符号（如红色心形）能够在看似无关的任务上强烈影响模型行为，例如在简单编程问题上引导模型倾向于递归解法。值得注意的是，这种引导效应在很大程度上是隐性的，因为模型对视觉符号的直接解读和思维轨迹与其观察到的实际行为存在显著差异。在模型之间的视觉交流中，这导致了一种“生成—解读”鸿沟：模型倾向于发送它们自己（以及人类）觉得直观的形状基元，但这些视觉线索往往无法有效引导其他模型。在涉及抽象概念和故事的进一步交流游戏中，模型能够创造性地使用视觉元素相互传递意义，尽管其中某些交流内容对人类而言仍不直观。
tldr: 研究发现视觉语言模型会被简单视觉符号隐性地引导行为（如心形符号引导模型采用递归解法），且模型间视觉交流存在“生成—解读”鸿沟——模型发送的直观视觉线索往往无法有效引导其他模型。
en_tdlr: The study reveals that VLMs can be implicitly steered by simple visual symbols (e.g., a heart symbol guiding models toward recursive solutions), and identifies a generation-interpretation gap in model-to-model visual communication, where intuitively shaped visual cues often fail to steer other models.
